subtopic: CPU vs GPU execution model contrasts
learningObjective: Compare CPU and GPU execution models on branch prediction, out-of-order execution, register file, and cache hierarchy design.
stem: Which statements correctly contrast the CPU and GPU execution models? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: CPUs devote substantial die area to branch prediction, out-of-order scheduling and large caches per core; GPUs devote proportionally more area to compute units and register files, using massive thread-level parallelism to hide memory latency instead.

GPUs typically have a much larger register file per SM than a CPU core has per core, because switching between many warps requires their register state to remain resident for zero-cost context switching.
CPU L1 caches are typically per-core and larger per thread than GPU L1/shared memory per thread, reflecting the CPU's reliance on temporal locality within a single thread.
GPUs do not use caches at all; latency hiding via warp switching removes any need for a cache hierarchy.

explanation: A: This is the canonical CPU-throughput vs GPU-throughput design philosophy, articulated in HP6/PMPP4. B: GPU register files (e.g., 65 K × 4 B per SM on A100 ≈ 256 KB) are much larger than CPU per-core register files (~2 KB architectural), enabling zero-cost warp switching. C: CPU L1D is ~32-48 KB per core with a small resident thread count; GPU L1/shared is up to 192 KB per SM but is shared across many threads, giving less per-thread capacity. D is wrong: modern GPUs have L1 (per SM) and L2 (per GPU) caches; latency hiding via warp switching complements, not replaces, caching.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: large register file enables zero-cost warp switching in SIMT.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: CPU L1 per-thread capacity is typically larger than GPU L1/shared per-thread capacity.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: GPUs have L1 and L2 caches; latency hiding complements rather than replaces caching.

assumptions: Standard modern CPU (Intel/AMD OoO) vs data-center GPU (NVIDIA Ampere/Hopper) comparison.
Rough die-area allocations and per-thread capacities as documented in whitepapers and PMPP4.
nonImplications: Does not imply CPUs cannot exploit DLP; SIMD ISAs like AVX-512 provide substantial DLP.
Does not imply GPUs never benefit from data locality; kernels still use shared memory and L1 for reuse.

distractorRationales.D: Fabricated 'no cache' claim contradicting decades of GPU architecture.
